parsed.g: Search for 'mouth night guard' listings and sort the results by descending price
P_t: Typed 'mouth night guard' into the search box and submitted the search (Step 1)
Search results page for 'mouth night guard' is displayed showing 9819 items
R_t: Select 'Price' as the sort criterion in the Sort By dropdown
Ensure the sort direction is set to descending (high to low)
parsed.e_t: The page is the search results page for 'mouth night guard' showing 12 of 9819 items. The Sort By select element (id='sorter') currently has 'Relevance' selected (selected='selected'). The direction switcher link has class 'sort-desc' and title 'Set Ascending Direction', meaning the current direction is descending. The 'Price' option in the sorter has value='price' and is NOT selected. The page is sorted by Relevance in descending order, not by Price. The toolbar uses a standard HTML select element for sorting, not a custom ARIA combobox menu.
C: The sort direction switcher currently shows 'Set Ascending Direction' (class='sort-desc'), meaning the current direction is already descending — so once Price is selected, no additional direction change should be needed
The Sort By control is a native HTML <select> element (id='sorter'), not a custom ARIA combobox with menu items

F_t.cause: The sort order did not change — DOM still shows 'Relevance' as selected='selected' in the <select id='sorter'>. The agent was clicking an ARIA menuitem representation, but the actual control is a native <select> element. The click did not trigger the sort change.
Same as Step 3 — DOM still shows 'Relevance' selected in <select id='sorter'>. Clicking the ARIA menuitem [3031] again did not change the sort order.
Clicking the combobox to open it did not result in the dropdown opening in a way that allowed selection — DOM still shows expanded: False and Relevance still selected.

DOM still shows <option value='relevance' selected='selected'> in the native <select id='sorter'>. The Price option remains unselected. Repeated clicks on the ARIA menuitem representation are not triggering the native select change.

K_t: The Sort By control is a native HTML <select> element with id='sorter' and data-role='sorter', containing options: 'name' (Product Name), 'price' (Price), 'relevance' (Relevance, currently selected)

The direction switcher link has class 'sort-desc' and title 'Set Ascending Direction', meaning the current sort direction is already descending — clicking Price should yield descending price sort without needing to change direction
The agent has been repeatedly clicking ARIA menuitem [3031] but the underlying DOM select element has not changed its selected value from 'relevance' to 'price'
The correct approach would be to use a 'select' action on the native <select id='sorter'> element to choose the 'price' option, rather than clicking ARIA menuitems
Total results: 9819 items for 'mouth night guard' search
The toolbar configuration shows directionDefault='desc', meaning descending is the default direction
